column1: # Cross-script Balochi lexicon: arabic <TAB> roman <TAB> ipa (full-voweled, Southern Balochi). Compiled from Korn
# (2005a) + Jahani & Korn (2009) + ASJP Southern-Balochi (bcc), prioritising words attested in ≥2 INDEPENDENT
# sources, then EXPANDED with the Korn Etymological Index (see the EXPANDED note below). Recovers the vowels the
# the Arabic phonemizer looks a word up by its Arabic spelling → full IPA (short vowels + the oː/uː, eː/iː quality);
# the Roman phonemizer looks it up by its roman spelling. OOV falls back to the per-script g2p. Sources per row: K=Korn,
# J=Jahani&Korn, A=ASJP(independent). Retroflex ʈ/ɖ from J (ASJP loses them). Grow from Korn's lexicon over time.
# EXPANDED: + 344 headwords auto-mined from Korn (2005a) Etymological Index (roman→IPA deterministic;
# Arabic keys reverse-transliterated, native-accurate/loanword-approximate; retroflex text-layer-limited — the 4
# PaddleOCR-flagged were image-verified: kabāṭ fixed to retroflex, 3 noise flags dropped). Roman path ASJP-corroborated ~97%.
# NUMERALS — Jahani & Korn (2009), "Balochi", in *The Iranian Languages*, TABLE 11.19 (CARDINAL NUMBERS), first
# (= most common) variant taken for each slot; magnitudes sad '100', hazār '1,000', lak(k) '100,000', kurōr
# '10,000,000', arab '1,000,000,000' from the same table (arab = 10^9 per FBB / Sayad Hashmi 2000, the reading J&K
# list first; BMC has 10^8). Roman → IPA by the standard Southern-Balochi correspondences already used above
# (dental t̪/d̪, unaspirated, r not ɽ). Read by balochi/numbers.ts; the Arabic abjad cannot recover these vowels on
# its own (هپت → *hpt̪), which is exactly what this lexicon exists for. NOT in J&K: sifr '0' (a Perso-Arabic loan —
# Table 11.19 starts at 1). Forms already present above are not repeated (yak, do, panč, šiš '6', duwāzdah '12',
# čārdah '14', nawad '90'); bīst '20' and sī '30' need no row (the g2p already yields biːst̪ / siː).
# HOMOGRAPH NOTE: ⟨سد⟩ is re-asserted here as sad '100' — it appears above BOTH as sad and (later, so previously
# winning) as sud 'profit'; the numeral is the commoner reading and the lexicon has no POS disambiguation. ⟨چل⟩ was
# left alone for the same reason and 40 uses the J&K variant čihil ⟨چهل⟩ instead of čil.
